$comment: Gemfall beat 7, the Tether's chapter 7 (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 7L). Three instruments are chapter props (tether_ledger, tether_chord, tether_question); honest ways to them are checks, double games are certain but cost a friend's trust (wardens_trust is set false when the party sells the wardens' secrets to the choir) or a stone. Every ending sets climbed_the_mountain. The seal clock is set once per path: scene_tether_holds (clock_steady), scene_tether_slips (clock_late), or ending_lost_in_echoes (clock_late, the lost-fight setback). facet_caravan is defined in gemfall-07h. Pacing episodes on the spine (the table's rule vote, the two scouts, the first sitting, the returning cart, the night visitor, the rope bridge, the crowds at the bend, who keeps the table) set only chapter-local flags; practiced, two_helpers and table_works open extra TN 12 ways into the test.
title: The Tether

objectives.label: Held the Caravan Stone's hum still for one whole breath
Kept the wardens' trust to the very end

tether_ledger.name: The Cage-Doctrine Ledger
tether_ledger.text: The wardens' plan for holding what is under the mountain. They do not lend it.

tether_chord.name: The Resonance Chord
tether_chord.text: Three notes the choir hums to make the stones hum back. Written down nowhere.

tether_question.name: The Witch's Question
tether_question.text: What do you actually want? A witch lent it to you. You may ask it of anything.

scene_the_table.narration: The wardens will not sit with the cult, the people in painted bark masks who follow Hessa from the soup tent. The masks will not sit with the wardens. So you build a table, out of an old door and two barrels, right in the middle of the Pinch, the one gap between two red hills that every road squeezes through, and sit at it yourselves. The ground shakes and the table wobbles, and somebody folds a sock under the short leg.

choices.label: Get the table ready
Ask the grandmothers to chair the table

scene_the_table_grandmothers_chair.narration: You ask a grandmother to chair the table. She brings her knitting, sits down at the head of your old door, and says nothing at all. Within a minute, a warden and a mask have both stopped shouting, because it is very hard to shout near a grandmother who is knitting. "Well?" she says. "Sit."

choices.label: Get the table ready

choice_the_rule.narration: A table between two sides needs one rule, chalked on the top where everyone can read it. Only one, or nobody will remember it. Wardens and masks are already drifting over to see what you write. What is the rule?

choices.label: Nobody shouts
Masks up and faces showing at the table
Everyone who sits brings one thing to share

choice_the_rule_no_shouting.narration: You chalk NOBODY SHOUTS across the middle of the door in big letters. Within five minutes a warden forgets and shouts, and everybody looks at the chalk, and then at him. He goes red, sits down, and pours the tea for everyone, which turns out to be the punishment.

choices.label: Go to the wardens

choice_the_rule_masks_up.narration: You chalk MASKS UP, FACES SHOWING. The masks look at each other for a long moment. Then a young one pushes hers up onto her head, and she has freckles, and the warden opposite blinks as if he had forgotten there were people under there. After that, the others do it too.

choices.label: Go to the wardens

choice_the_rule_bring_one.narration: You chalk BRING ONE THING TO SHARE. By noon the table holds a warden's biscuit tin, a pot of the masks' soup, a pencil, a lump of honeycomb, and a very old map nobody can read. People sit down just to see what is on it. That was the idea.

choices.label: Go to the wardens

scene_ledger.narration: The wardens' cage doctrine lives in a ledger as thick as a doorstep, chained to a desk, and the desk is guarded by Pellam, who has never once smiled on duty and has logged that fact twice. "Not for lending," says Pellam, before you have said anything at all.

choices.label: You told the wardens first. Ask as a friend.
Make the honest case
Promise them the cult's secret chord in trade (you won't)

scene_ledger_false_promise.narration: You promise him the masks' secret chord in trade. You do not mean it, and Pellam writes down the promise anyway, in full, and makes you watch him do it. The ledger is heavy in your arms all the way up the valley, and it is not the pages that make it heavy.

choices.label: Up the valley to the choir

scene_ledger_friend.narration: "We told you first," you say. "We're asking as friends." Pellam looks at the chain for a long time. Then he unlocks it, and writes LENT in a column that has never had anything written in it. "Bring it back," he says. "I shall know if a page is bent."

choices.label: Up the valley to the choir

check_ledger.prompt: Show Pellam why a cage needs a key-holder

onSuccess.narration: Pellam reads your argument twice, frowns at it twice, and unlocks the chain. Nobody has ever seen Pellam do that. Nobody has ever seen Pellam almost smile, either, and he very nearly does.

onFailure.narration: Pellam listens politely and says no politely. The ledger stays chained to its desk. You leave with nothing but a very clear picture of the cover.

scene_two_scouts.narration: Halfway up the side valley, two people step out onto the path at once, from opposite sides: a young warden cadet called Linnet, and a young mask called Rook. They glare at each other. Then they both turn to you. "What did the other lot give you?" they say together, and then glare at each other for saying it together.

choices.label: Tell them both the truth
Tell each one what they want to hear
Set the Table Stone down between them

check_two_scouts.prompt: Tell two suspicious scouts the same true story at the same time

onSuccess.narration: You tell them both everything, the same way, at the same time. They listen with their arms folded. By the end their arms are not folded. Linnet holds out her hand. Rook looks at it as if it might bite, then shakes it.

onFailure.narration: You tell them the truth. They do not believe a word of it, and both stomp off to tell their bosses. But they stomp off the same way, and the last you see of them, they are arguing in a way that sounds a lot like talking.

scene_two_scouts_fib.narration: You tell Linnet what a warden wants to hear, and Rook what a mask wants to hear. Both of them go away happy. Later, from higher up the valley, you see them sitting on the same rock, comparing notes. They both look up at you at exactly the same moment.

choices.label: Up the valley to the choir

scene_two_scouts_table_stone.narration: You set the Table Stone down on the path, the stone from the truth-table at Redspire, logged twice. It hums. Linnet knows it from the citadel. Rook knows the note from the choir. They crouch on either side of it, listening, and forget to glare. "It's the same stone," says Rook. "It's the same stone," says Linnet.

choices.label: Up the valley to the choir

scene_choir.narration: Up a side valley, Hessa's soup-tent people, the ones who call themselves the Deep Hollow, are humming in a ring with painted bark masks pushed up on their heads. They are singing the stones' own note, and the stones in your packs hum along, as if they know the words.

choices.label: Ask to learn it, and tell them why
Ask the grandmothers to vouch for you
Trade them the wardens' cage plans, page by page
Pay them with a stone from your pack
Hum along until they forget you are not one of them

scene_choir_hum_along.narration: Your kitsune hums along, badly at first and then not badly at all, until the choir forgets your kitsune is not one of them and sings the whole chord out plain. Three notes. Your kitsune hums them all the way back down the valley, very quietly, and nobody comes after you.

choices.label: Back to the table

scene_choir_pay_stone.narration: You pay with a stone from your pack. The choir passes it from hand to hand, humming, and the stone hums back, and then it is in a sack and gone. They teach you the chord. The pack is one stone lighter and you can feel exactly where it used to sit.

choices.label: Back to the table

scene_choir_sell_secrets.narration: You trade them the wardens' cage plans, page by page, and Hessa reads each one with her lips moving. "Pellam will know," she says, not unkindly, and teaches you the chord in return, three notes that stay in your head like a tune you did not choose. The ledger feels lighter now, and that is not a good feeling.

choices.label: Back to the table

scene_choir_vouch.narration: The grandmother hums with them. Not the chord, just a low knitting sort of hum, and the choir softens around it the way a room softens when somebody's nan comes in. "Teach them," she says, and they do, slowly, three notes, until you have them.

choices.label: Back to the table

check_chord.prompt: Convince a choir of masks to teach their chord to people who want to hold the seal, not break it

onSuccess.narration: The choir argues in whispers. Then Hessa, the soup-line lady, steps forward and hums three notes, slowly, until you have them. "Don't make me sorry," she says.

onFailure.narration: They sing it for you once, very fast, and then pull their masks down. You remember the first note. Only the first.

scene_first_sitting.narration: Back at the table, it finally happens: Pellam sits down on one side, and Hessa sits down on the other. Nobody speaks. Then the ground shrugs, the sock shoots out from under the short leg, and the whole table tips toward Pellam. Hessa grabs her soup. Pellam grabs his ledger. Everyone looks at you.

choices.label: Fix the wobbly leg properly
Swap seats, and take the wobbly side yourselves
Look at the grandmother

check_first_sitting.prompt: Fix a wobbly table while two sides watch you do it

onSuccess.narration: A flat stone, a bit of string and a lot of squinting. The table stands dead level. Pellam tests it with his pencil, which does not roll. Hessa tests it with her soup, which does not spill. They both nod, at the table, which is nearly the same as nodding at each other.

onFailure.narration: You fix it. Now it wobbles toward Hessa instead. You fix it again. Now it wobbles both ways at once. Pellam makes a small noise that might be a laugh, and Hessa definitely laughs, and somehow, after that, they both stay sitting down.

scene_first_sitting_wobbly_side.narration: You swap seats and sit on the wobbly side yourselves, with your elbows holding it level. It is not comfortable. Pellam notices. Hessa notices. Neither of them says anything, but both of them lean in a little, the way people do when somebody else has taken the worst chair.

choices.label: Hold the table steady

scene_first_sitting_grandmother.narration: You look at the grandmother. The grandmother looks at the table leg. Without dropping a stitch, she puts out one foot and rests it under the short corner, and leaves it there for the rest of the afternoon. Nobody, warden or mask, dares to tip the table after that.

choices.label: Hold the table steady

scene_road_gifts.narration: Back at your wobbly table, something strange starts happening. The road begins bringing things back to you: things you did on the way here, walking up the hill on their own legs, as if the whole realm had been keeping your receipts.

choices.label: A flat boat is coming up the dry creek
A MossHome runner is waving a knotted cord
A boggart is sidling up with a satchel
A boggart is sidling up with a satchel
Mother Thrum from the ford is here, with a ringing sock
Visit the witch's stall at the end of the road

scene_ossley.narration: A frog in a very old hat is poling a flat boat up a creek with no water in it: the frog from the reeds of the Great River, with OLD OSSLEY painted on the side of his boat, and a boat full of every stone the river took off somebody this season. He looks at your packs, and listens to you hum, and says: "Leashes are for things that want to run." Then he says nothing for quite a while.

choices.label: Ask what you still owe him from the river
Thank him, and go and find the witch

scene_ossley_debt.narration: Ossley's price is not coin. It never was. "Whatever you tie," he says, "tie it with a knot you can undo." He makes you show him the knot, there and then, on his boat rope. It takes three tries.

choices.label: Promise

scene_mosshome_runner.narration: A MossHome runner jogs up with a string of grumbling mules carrying everything the Woods confiscated from careless hunters. She counts the knots on your cord, unloads it all, and passes on one message from the elders: "Whatever you are tying, tie it loose."

choices.label: Thank her, and the Woods

scene_boggart.narration: A boggart with a satchel of scribbled paper sidles up, not looking at you, and says to nobody: "Catalog. Who bought what. Who sold to who. Costs one really good sentence you overheard."

choices.label: Tell it what Pellam mutters to his ledger
Tell it what the choir hums when nobody is listening

scene_boggart_choir_said.narration: You hum what the choir hums when nobody is listening, which is the same three notes, only sadder. The boggart goes completely still and listens with its whole body. "Sidelong," it says at last, approvingly, and hands over the catalog without ever once looking at you.

choices.label: Go and find the witch's stall

scene_boggart_brisk_said.narration: You tell it what Pellam mutters to his ledger when he thinks nobody is listening, which is mostly numbers and once, very quietly, "oh dear." The boggart hugs itself. "A clerk's oh dear," it tells nobody. "Rarer than rubies." The catalog is in your hands before you notice it has let go.

choices.label: Go and find the witch's stall

scene_ford_witch.narration: Mother Thrum, the witch from the ford queue, has come all the way up the road with a wool sock under one arm, and something in it is ringing. "I always ask twice," she says. "Once at the ford, and once at the mountain. What do you actually want?"

choices.label: "To hold it still, so nobody gets hurt."
"To hold it, because we can."
Say whatever will get you the question

scene_ford_witch_flatter.narration: You say whatever you think will get you the question. Mother Thrum listens to all of it with her head on one side. "No," she says, pleasantly, when you finish. "That's not a want. That's a wish for a want." She lends you nothing, and her charms ring once, as if amused.

choices.label: Back toward the table

scene_ford_witch_hold_power.narration: "To hold it, because we can." Mother Thrum does not look away. "Honest," she says. "I'll give you honest." She lends you the question anyway, but she holds onto it a heartbeat longer than she needs to before she lets go. "Ask it of yourselves first," she says.

choices.label: Back toward the table

scene_ford_witch_hold_safe.narration: "To hold it still, so nobody gets hurt." Mother Thrum looks at you for a long moment, and then nods, once. "That one I'll lend," she says, and presses the question into your hands like a small warm coin. "Ask it of anything. Even me." Then she tips the ringing thing out of her sock as well, a stone from the ford, and it goes quiet in your hand.

choices.label: Back toward the table

scene_stall_witch.narration: At the end of the road a witch in a patched hat runs a remedy stall, and every charm on it is ringing by itself. "I'll lend you my question," she says, "if you answer it first. What do you actually want?"

choices.label: "To hold it still, so nobody gets hurt."
"To hold it, because we can."
Say whatever will get you the question

scene_stall_witch_flatter.narration: You say whatever you think will get you the question. The stall witch listens to all of it with her head on one side. "No," she says, pleasantly, when you finish. "That's not a want. That's a wish for a want." She lends you nothing, and her charms ring once, as if amused.

choices.label: Back toward the table

scene_stall_witch_hold_power.narration: "To hold it, because we can." The stall witch does not look away. "Honest," she says. "I'll give you honest." She lends you the question anyway, but she holds onto it a heartbeat longer than she needs to before she lets go. "Ask it of yourselves first," she says.

choices.label: Back toward the table

scene_stall_witch_hold_safe.narration: "To hold it still, so nobody gets hurt." The stall witch looks at you for a long moment, and then nods, once. "That one I'll lend," she says, and presses the question into your hands like a small warm coin. "Ask it of anything. Even me."

choices.label: Back toward the table

scene_returning_cart.narration: On the way back, a grandmothers' cart full of stones going home has stuck on the steep bit, and the grandmother pushing it is very small. But tomorrow is the test at the bend, and none of you has ever held a hum still in your life. There is one afternoon left. Help with the cart, or practice?

choices.label: Help push the cart up the hill
Practice on a small stone instead
Push one-handed and practice with the other

check_returning_cart.prompt: Push a cart full of stones up the steep bit

onSuccess.narration: Shoulders down, everybody push. The cart groans up the steep bit and over the top. The grandmother gives you each a warm bead from her apron, and says, "Practice tonight, dears. You'll need it."

onFailure.narration: The cart rolls back two steps for every three you push it. In the end you sit on the back of it like a seesaw while the grandmother pulls, and between you it gets over the top. She laughs so hard she has to sit down.

scene_returning_cart_practice.narration: You leave the cart to a passing warden and find a quiet rock. You hold a small humming stone between your hands and try to make it still. It takes all afternoon. Then, for half a breath, it stops. You all feel it at once, like a held door. Behind you, the cart gets up the hill without you.

choices.label: Back to the table

scene_returning_cart_both.narration: Your bigfoot puts one enormous hand on the cart and pushes it up the hill as if it were a pram, while holding a small humming stone in the other hand and frowning at it. Halfway up, the stone goes still for half a breath. The grandmother says she has never seen anything like it, and she has seen a lot.

choices.label: Back to the table

scene_evening.narration: Evening. Campfires pop up all along the road, and the wardens' fires and the masks' fires are as far apart as they can possibly get. Your table is exactly in the middle. Somebody has left a cup of tea on it, and nobody will say who.

choices.label: A centaur relay is cantering in with news
Listen to the singers at the campfires
An Exchange caravan rolls in, and someone is waving
Walk the dark road between the two sides' fires
Sleep under the table

scene_evening_between.narration: You walk the dark strip of road between the wardens' fires and the masks' fires. On one side, somebody is singing a counting song. On the other, somebody is singing the same tune with different words. Neither side knows. You stand in the middle and hear both at once, and it sounds like one song.

choices.label: Back to the table

scene_centaur_relay.narration: The centaur relay pulls up at your table and unrolls a sash-map. "Fat caravan tomorrow, biggest stone in the funnel," says the lead runner. "Where do you want it?" You point at the worst bend, and she nods as if that is the most sensible thing anyone has said all day.

choices.label: Thank the relay and get some sleep

scene_relay_sing.narration: The relay singers have new verses about wagons that have not arrived yet, so you hear tomorrow's traffic tonight. Then a grandmother's runner brings you a list of caves nobody may ever dig. It is exactly the list a seal's keeper would keep.

choices.label: Fold the list away and get some sleep

scene_ember.narration: "Darlings! From the docks!" Madame Coralie Fenn is lashed to the top of the caravan in her barrel on wheels, waving with both arms. She remembers you fondly. She also remembers the warm red stone you sold her on the quay, your very first one. It is right here in a velvet box with a new label, THE EMBER FACET, and its price has gone up a very great deal since then.

choices.label: Buy it back. A tether needs an anchor.
Wave, and let it go on its way

scene_ember_wave.narration: You wave. Madame Fenn waves back with both arms and the barrel wobbles alarmingly on its lashings. "Next time, darlings!" she calls, and the caravan rolls on toward the camps with your very first stone humming in a velvet box on top of it. You watch until the lanterns turn the corner.

choices.label: Find somewhere to sleep

scene_ember_buy_back.narration: You pay what Madame Fenn asks, which is a great deal, and she counts it twice and hugs the velvet box before she hands it over. "I always hoped it would be you, darlings," she says, and seems to mean it. The Ember Facet is warm as toast, exactly as you remember, and it hums as if it remembers you too.

choices.label: Find somewhere to sleep

scene_night_visitor.narration: Late at night, Pellam comes to your table alone, with no ledger under his arm for once. He sits down carefully on the steady side. "One question," he says quietly. "Where does the choir sing at night? I only want to know." Across the road, a mask's fire crackles, and somebody over there is very still.

choices.label: Tell him
Tell him it isn't yours to tell
Wave Hessa over, and let them ask each other

scene_night_visitor_tell.narration: You tell him. Pellam writes it down twice and thanks you, very politely, and goes back to the warden fires. Across the road, the still mask gets up and goes into a tent, and does not come out again. Nobody says anything about it in the morning. Nobody has to.

choices.label: Sleep under the table

scene_night_visitor_not_mine.narration: "It isn't ours to tell," you say. Pellam looks at you for a long moment. Then he nods, takes out a small notebook, and writes one word in it. You lean over to read it. The word is FAIR. He underlines it twice and goes back to bed.

choices.label: Sleep under the table

check_night_visitor.prompt: Get a warden clerk and a choir singer to ask each other their own questions

onSuccess.narration: Hessa comes over with two cups of soup. Pellam takes one. They talk until the fire is embers, about the mountain, and the rules, and which of them is more tired. When they go back to their own sides, they say goodnight to each other. Out loud.

onFailure.narration: Hessa comes over, but she and Pellam sit at opposite ends and only talk to you. "Ask him why," says Hessa. "Ask her what for," says Pellam. You pass the questions back and forth until midnight. It is slow. It is still talking.

rest_under_the_table.narration: You sleep under your own wobbly table, between the wardens' fires and the masks' fires. In the night a warden and a mask both come over to borrow the teapot at the same moment, and stand there not looking at each other until somebody says please. Patch each other up. The teapot survives.

choices.label: Up the switchback to the bend

scene_rope_bridge.narration: On the way to the switchback, the road crosses a deep gully on a rope bridge. It was a perfectly good bridge yesterday. Today, every time the ground shrugs, it swings gently from side to side, like a hammock with opinions. A snowhorn goat is standing in the middle of it, chewing, refusing to go either way.

choices.label: Cross one at a time, quick and light
Tie yourselves together and go slowly
Tie on with a knot you can undo, the way you were told

check_rope_bridge.prompt: Dash across a swinging bridge between tremors

onSuccess.narration: You wait for the swing to settle, then go, one, two, three, light as leaves. The goat watches you squeeze past it, chews thoughtfully, and follows you off the far end, as if that had been its plan all along.

onFailure.narration: Halfway over, the ground shrugs and the bridge swings, and you end up clinging to the goat, who does not mind at all. When it stops swinging, the goat walks you the rest of the way across, very slowly, like a nanny.

scene_rope_bridge_roped.narration: You rope yourselves together, front to back, and go over so slowly that a snail would be embarrassed. When the bridge swings, you all lean the same way at once, without even saying. Being tied to each other turns out to feel a lot like being a team. The goat lets you pass.

choices.label: Up to the switchback

scene_rope_bridge_loose_knot.narration: You tie yourselves to the handrail with a loose knot, the kind you can undo. Every few steps, you undo it and tie it again further along. It is slow, and very safe, and by the far side you could tie that knot in your sleep. Which was, you suspect, the point.

choices.label: Up to the switchback

scene_switchback.narration: Halfway up the switchback the road runs through a narrow cutting, and something in the cutting is repeating every sound you make, half a breath late. Your footsteps. Your whispers. Your humming stones. With it, a lone cinder wolf, coming down off the mountain with its ears flat.

choices.label: Make a racket, all of you at once
Face whatever it is
Follow the trail of tiny tied grass knots around the cutting
Fly up and over the cutting

scene_switchback_fly_over.narration: You go up and over the cutting, and the echo hunter repeats the sound of your wings to the rocks, half a breath late, and gets very confused about which way you went. The wolf has already gone. You come down on the far side with your humming stones still rattling in your packs.

choices.label: On to the worst bend

scene_switchback_sprite_knots.narration: Tiny knots of grass, tied at ankle height, lead off the road and over the top of the cutting. Harvest sprites, this far north, still looking out for you. You follow the knots, and the echo below you repeats your footsteps to an empty road.

choices.label: On to the worst bend

check_echoes.prompt: Make the cutting so noisy the echo cannot pick one sound to follow

onSuccess.narration: Clapping, stamping, humming, one terrible whistle. The echo hunter cannot choose, gets a headache, and backs off into the rocks. The wolf, who hates the noise even more, runs straight past you.

onFailure.narration: Somebody stops a moment too early, and in the silence the echo hunter hears exactly one heartbeat. Yours.

encounter_echoes.narration: The echo hunter unfolds out of the rock wall, and the wolf, frightened half silly, sticks close beside it.

onVictory.narration: The echo hunter folds itself back into the rock, sulking, and the wolf bolts down the hill. The cutting is just a cutting again.

onDefeat.narration: The echoes get louder and louder until you cannot hear yourselves think. You stumble back down the switchback the way you came, and your humming stones rattle loose in your packs.

scene_bend_crowds.narration: At the worst bend, both sides got there first. Wardens are stacking numbered boxes on one side of the road. Masks are unrolling sacks on the other. Both are planning to grab the Caravan Stone the moment it arrives, which would end your test before it starts. Far below, the caravan is coming.

choices.label: Draw a line across the road: nobody crosses until you try
Ask each side for one helper
Wave to Linnet and Rook

scene_bend_crowds_chalk_line.narration: You draw a chalk line right across the road and stand on it. "One breath," you say. "Give us one breath to try. Then you can argue." The wardens look at the masks. The masks look at the wardens. Neither side wants to be the one who crossed the line first, so nobody does.

choices.label: Wait for the caravan

check_bend_crowds.prompt: Talk both sides into lending you one helper each

onSuccess.narration: A warden steps over, and then, after a long pause, a mask. They stand on either side of you, not looking at each other, ready to help. It is the first time all season they have stood on the same bit of road.

onFailure.narration: Both sides send their grumpiest. The two of them argue about where to stand until the caravan is nearly here. But while they are arguing, nobody else grabs anything, which is almost as good.

scene_bend_crowds_scouts.narration: Linnet and Rook come running from opposite ends of the bend and stand beside you, one on each side. The wardens stare. The masks stare. Then, slowly, both sides put down their boxes and sacks, because their own people are standing with you, and you cannot grab something out from under your own people.

choices.label: Wait for the caravan

choice_the_test.narration: At the worst bend, the fattest caravan in the funnel is coming, and the stone in its middle wagon hums so loudly the mules wear earmuffs. If you can hold that one stone's hum still for one breath, you can hold anything. Wardens on one side, masks on the other, both watching you.

choices.label: Ask the stone the witch's question
The relay sent the caravan right to you. Be ready.
You heard this caravan in last night's song. Be ready.
The catalog says whose stone it is. Ask them first.
Tie it with a knot you can undo
Follow the cage doctrine, page by page
Hum the choir's chord
You practiced on a small stone. You know the feeling.
A warden and a mask hold on with you
Pellam and Hessa both nod to you to begin
Hold it with nothing but nerve

check_hold_easy.prompt: Ask the Caravan Stone what it actually wants, and listen for the answer

onSuccess.narration: You ask the witch's question out loud. The stone goes quiet, the way a person goes quiet when somebody finally asks the right thing. For one long breath, nothing on the whole hillside hums at all.

onFailure.narration: You ask the question, but the ground lurches halfway through and the stone never hears the end of it. The hum leaps free, and the whole hillside answers it.

check_hold.prompt: Hold the Caravan Stone's hum still for one whole breath

onSuccess.narration: For one long breath the humming stops. The mules take their earmuffs off. The wardens stop writing. The masks stop humming. Then it starts again, softer, as if it is listening to you.

onFailure.narration: You almost have it. Then the hum slides through your fingers like a fish, and the whole hillside answers it.

check_hold_hard.prompt: Hold the Caravan Stone's hum still with no instruments at all

onSuccess.narration: No ledger, no chord, no question. Just you, holding on. And for one long breath, astonishingly, it is enough.

onFailure.narration: It is like trying to hold a thunderstorm in a teacup. The hum leaps free, and the whole hillside answers it.

scene_tether_holds.narration: The caravan master climbs down, hands you the Caravan Stone in both arms, and says, "Please keep it. It's been humming at me for a month." A warden writes something in a notebook. A mask takes off her mask. For a moment, everyone is looking at the same thing: you.

choices.label: Go back to the table one last time

scene_tether_slips.narration: The hum jumps free, and the ground answers with a long, rolling shake. In the muddle the masks drive the middle wagon away up a side track, apologizing as they go. The tremors do not stop after that. They settle into a slow, patient rhythm, like a drum.

choices.label: Go back to the table one last time

scene_who_keeps_table.narration: Before you climb, you go back down to the Pinch one last time. Your old door is still there on its two barrels, chalk and all. People are packing up and running. But somebody has to keep the table while you are up the mountain, or there will be nothing to come back to. Who?

choices.label: Ask Pellam and Hessa to keep it together
Give it to the grandmothers
Whistle down the dry creek for the frog from the river

check_who_keeps_table.prompt: Ask two old rivals to look after one table

onSuccess.narration: Pellam looks at Hessa. Hessa looks at Pellam. Then they each take one end of the old door and lift it together. "Mind the short leg," says Hessa. "I've logged the short leg," says Pellam. They carry it down the hill side by side.

onFailure.narration: They cannot agree whose end is the front. In the end they carry it down the hill sideways, both talking at once. But they carry it together, and they do not put it down.

scene_who_keeps_table_grandmother.narration: You give the table to the grandmothers. Two of them tip it up, tuck it under their arms like a tray, and carry it off downhill, still knitting. "We'll keep your chalk on it, dear," one of them calls back. "Somebody will want reminding."

choices.label: Turn and climb

scene_who_keeps_table_ossley.narration: A frog in a very old hat comes poling his flat boat up the dry creek, as if he had been waiting to be asked: the frog from the reeds of the Great River, with OLD OSSLEY painted on his boat. He looks at the table for a long time, and then lays it across his boat like a roof. "Tables float," he says. That is all he says. The boat slides away down a creek with no water in it, carrying your table somewhere safe.

choices.label: Turn and climb

rest_up_the_mountain.narration: At the tree line you look back. Wardens, masks, wagons and mules are all running downhill, together for once. There is not a single embermoth left in the foothills. You turn around and walk up the mountain everyone else is running away from, carrying whatever you managed to borrow, a ledger or a chord or a question, and a great deal of nerve.

ending_lost_in_echoes.narration: By the time the echoes let you go and you find the road again, the fattest caravan has long gone by, and the ground is shaking in a slow, patient rhythm. Nobody is at the table any more. You climb anyway, a long way behind, humming to yourselves to keep your courage up.

llmHints.tone: warm, clever, a little spooky but never scary; two rival groups and the party as the table between them
forbidden: saying what is under the mountain

npcVoices.hessa: Deep Hollow choir member who ran the soup tent; gentle, wary, wants to trust you
npcVoices.old_ossley: very few words, long pauses that are not hesitation, answers the question you meant
npcVoices.mosshome_runner: breathless, cheerful, counts knots out loud
npcVoices.boggart: talks sidelong to nobody, never meets your eye, treasures overheard sentences
npcVoices.ford_witch: Mother Thrum, the ford witch; pointed hat, dry, kind underneath; only asks one question and means it
npcVoices.stall_witch: patched hat, brisk, charms ringing around her; lends questions, never sells them
npcVoices.centaur_relay: brisk, proud of the roads, delighted to be asked where something should go
npcVoices.exchange_merchant: Madame Coralie Fenn, the Exchange gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; delighted to see you, genuinely fond, calls everyone darlings, and still a merchant
npcVoices.caravan_master: exhausted, practical, has had a headache since the stone came aboard
npcVoices.pellam: Pellam, warden ledger clerk; writes everything down twice, never smiles on duty, says no politely and means it; secretly fair
npcVoices.linnet: Cadet Linnet, a young warden scout; keen, stiff, trying to look older, softens fast
npcVoices.rook: Rook, a young mask scout from the choir; prickly, quick, curious under it
